text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: PRIVATE-CONTROLPLANE-DEGRADED for customer AcmeCorp (vpc-54a). Severity: P1. Trigger: control-plane API latency > 5s and agent heartbeats missing. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incident/INC-9923

pagerduty: Incident INC-9923 fired and routed to oncall: Kenji (oncall).

Kenji (oncall): Acking. I see repeated 5xx spikes from control-plane in eu-west-1 and missing heartbeats for hosts in customer VPC (10.12.0.0/16). Starting initial triage.

Maya (SRE): @Kenji thanks. Can you paste the agent heartbeat grep and control-plane healthcheck output? I'll check infra metrics and LB health.

Kenji (oncall): Logs attached below (snippet):
```
2026-03-14T09:10:03Z agent-heartbeat vpc-54a host=acme-node-3 status=NO_HEARTBEAT
2026-03-14T09:10:05Z cp-api eu-west-1 latency_ms=5200 resp=503
2026-03-14T09:11:12Z agent-heartbeat vpc-54a host=acme-node-7 status=NO_HEARTBEAT
```

Dominic (eng-runtime): I'm seeing a surge in control-plane CPU on cp-01-eu and cp-02-eu. Kernel oom-events? Not yet. Network graphs show a flapping route to the customer's peering connection around 09:09-09:12. Could be partial network blackhole.

Lina (support): Heads-up: Customer AcmeCorp SREs just pinged support saying their service is failing with 503s. They've opened a ticket referencing INC-9923. They're asking for ETA.

Maya (SRE): Ok runbook steps: 1) confirm agent process status on affected hosts 2) validate control-plane node health 3) check route tables & peering status 4) if peering flap persists, failover control-plane to standby in eu-central-1 and inform customer.

Kenji (oncall): I'm SSHing to customer-facing agent proxy (via jump):
```
ssh jump-eu; ssh acme-node-3
sudo systemctl status redwood-agent
journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200 | grep -i error
```

Kenji (oncall): Agent on acme-node-3 shows redwood-agent crashed with OOM killer: "Killed process 21456 (redwood-agent) total-vm:2.1G". Memory spike correlates with sudden request storm. acme-node-7 similar.

Dominic (eng-runtime): If agents are OOM'ing, they will stop heartbeating which explains control-plane marking hosts missing. We should restart agents with constrained memory and enable backpressure. I'll prepare a patched systemd override to restart with --memory-limit=700M.

Maya (SRE): Before wide restart, let's mitigate customer impact: 1) add temporary rate-limit at frontend LB for AcmeCorp to smooth traffic 2) promote standby control-plane in eu-central to accept traffic 3) coordinate rolling restart of agents with lina on support to notify customer.

Lina (support): I'll DM AcmeCorp SRE with a short update: "We saw an agent/process OOM causing missing heartbeats and control-plane errors. We're applying mitigations (LB rate-limit + standby failover) and will do rolling restarts. ETA initial mitigation ~15m"

Kenji (oncall): Applying step 1: updating LB rule via infra-cli:
```
infra-cli lb update --name acme-front --rate-limit 100rps --dry-run=false
```

incident-bot: Action logged: LB rate-limit applied to acme-front (100 rps).

Dominic (eng-runtime): Initiating control-plane failover to eu-central-standby. Command: `cpctl promote --target eu-central-1 --id cp-standby-03 --force --reason "eu-west degraded"`. Performing canary traffic shift (10% -> 50%).

Maya (SRE): Monitoring control-plane sync. Also watch KV cache replication lag. If KV lag > 30s then rollback.

Kenji (oncall): Rolling restart agents on acme nodes one at a time with new memory limit. Command used:
```
sudo systemctl stop redwood-agent
sudo rm -f /var/tmp/redis-cache/*
sudo systemctl set-environment REDWOOD_AGENT_MEM=700M
sudo systemctl start redwood-agent
```

Kenji (oncall): acme-node-3 agent back up and heartbeating. cp API 503s dropped to 2xx for that host.

Lina (support): Updated customer: "We've applied a temporary rate-limit and are performing rolling restarts of your agents. You may see brief reconnections. We'll follow up when fully restored."

Maya (SRE): Control-plane promotion appears healthy. KV replication lag at 4s. Canary traffic at 25% with no errors. Proceed to 50%.

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: escalated to eng-runtime (Dominic) due to potential runtime patch.

Dominic (eng-runtime): Pushing a config change to agent service to enable memory cgroup enforcement cluster-wide. This will be a deferred rollout to avoid disrupting small customers. Creating a patch in the A/B rollout channel after this thread.

Kenji (oncall): After rolling restart of 5/6 affected hosts, control-plane 5xxs are back to baseline. Heartbeats restored for all previously missing nodes.

Lina (support): Customer confirms their app returned to normal. "Thanks for the quick response — looks good on our side."

Maya (SRE): I'll keep monitoring for 30m then close. Also open a followup ticket for postmortem: root cause likely unbounded memory growth in redwood-agent under high request concurrency. Need analysis: reproduce with load test and ship memory cap + backpressure.

Kenji (oncall): Marking incident as acknowledged -> mitigated. Updating incident record with actions and host-level logs.

pagerduty: Incident INC-9923 status changed: Acknowledged -> Resolved (mitigated) by Kenji (oncall). Resolution summary: agent OOMs caused missing heartbeats and control-plane pressure; mitigations: LB rate-limit, control-plane failover, rolling agent restarts with memory limits.

Maya (SRE): Postmortem owners: Dominic (eng-runtime) for agent fix, Kenji (oncall) for runbook updates, Lina (support) for customer comms. I'll create the postmortem doc and link it here.

Kenji (oncall): Closing thread. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
